name: Pan-Iranism
summary: Pan-Iranism is an Iranian nationalist ideology calling for cultural, linguistic and historical solidarity among the Iranian peoples of the Iranian plateau and its surroundings. It arose in the 1920s as a defence of Iran's territorial integrity against Pan-Turkism and Pan-Arabism, and its mainstream form today stresses cultural integration, while radical strands seek territorial reunification of Iranian-inhabited lands. It favours a strong centralised state, Persian as the common language, pride in pre-Islamic civilisation and a secular outlook hostile to clerical influence.
scope: The profile represents the mainstream Iranian Pan-Iranism of Mahmud Afshar and his journal Ayandeh (from 1925) and of the Pan-Iranist Party (founded in the 1940s, led by Mohsen Pezeshkpour), with Iranshahr-circle cultural nationalism as background. It excludes the separate Mellat Iran offshoot and Tajik or Armenian variants. Since the movement has no economic programme, most economic and social answers are low-confidence inferences.

universal-healthcare.rationale: No Pan-Iranist source addresses health policy; the movement is defined by national unity, not welfare, so it is split or indifferent.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Economic distribution is outside the movement's documented concerns; the party is described only as right-wing nationalist.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Afshar wanted a "national economy" backing a strong state, but neither he nor the party is documented as pro- or anti-market.

public-ownership.rationale: Afshar's emphasis on a national economy as the base of state power does not clearly imply public ownership of utilities.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No documented position; Pan-Iranism is a cultural-territorial nationalism indifferent to tax rates.

unions-good.rationale: Labour organisation is not a Pan-Iranist theme; Pezeshkpour's party opposed alliances with non-nationalist groups, but that is not a union stance.

property-fundamental.rationale: The movement left property rights unaddressed, so no stance can be derived beyond its right-wing label.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are not documented as favouring either deregulation or tighter control.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare was no part of the movement's agenda; indifferent.

worker-ownership.rationale: The party was a nationalist, right-wing and historically anti-leftist organisation, so collective worker ownership is inferred as foreign to it.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Party was accused of SAVAK ties but adherents did not articulate a doctrine on surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the party's disciplined, uniformed, nationalist-moralist style under Pezeshkpour; no explicit source.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; the movement was itself accused of ethnic chauvinism, but no stance on speech law is documented.

strong-leader.rationale: Afshar called for a strong, authoritative central state, while distinguishing it from despotism; Pezeshkpour's party was authoritarian in structure.

state-harmful.rationale: Afshar made a powerful central state a pillar of reviving Iranian civilization, so anarchist rejection of the state is alien.

limit-guns.rationale: Not a Pan-Iranist issue; no documented stance.

empower-police-military.rationale: The party used military ranks and uniforms and cooperated with the Pahlavi state, favouring a strong security apparatus to protect territorial integrity.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the secular-nationalist party's disciplined social conservatism; no explicit source.

decide-locally.rationale: Afshar insisted on a strong central government and Persian-language uniformity as foundations of national unity, against decentralising claims.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal policy is not addressed in Pan-Iranist sources.

traditional-family.rationale: The movement says nothing about family structure; secular modernists in Iranshahr even campaigned for women's education.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from an early-20th-century nationalist movement with no liberal social agenda.

abortion-legal.rationale: None of the Pan-Iranist sources touch abortion, and a movement about Iranian unity gives no basis to pick a side, so it is left neutral.

more-religion-public.rationale: The party today is defined by opposition to the post-1979 government's pan-Islamism and Islam's influence on Iranian culture, and is listed as favouring state secularism.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Redress of racial injustice is not on its agenda; Pan-Iranism stresses Iranian unity over group claims, so mild disagreement is inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Pan-Iranism's sources deal with nation, language and territory, not gender theory, so there is no position to infer.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Cultural integration of the Iranian peoples and defence of Iranian heritage are the core of Pan-Iranism.

gradual-change.rationale: The movement favoured rapid nationalist modernisation, like the Pahlavi state it fed, rather than slow deference to institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not documented; the movement is concerned with Iranian peoples across borders, not immigration into Iran.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The party's emblem (a crossed-out equals sign) says each nation must pursue its own interests against the great powers, implying scepticism of international bodies.

free-trade.rationale: The sources show economic nationalism around a national economy, but nothing about trade liberalisation, so the answer is neutral.

nation-first.rationale: The party's symbol and nationalist platform assert that each nation must pursue its own interests rather than accept unequal relations with major powers.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred from anti-great-power sovereignty stance; not explicitly addressed.

open-borders.rationale: A nationalist ideology centred on Iranian cultural-civilizational unity rejects open borders, though it seeks fluid ties among Iranian peoples.

limit-growth.rationale: Environmental limits are outside the movement.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate policy post-dates the movement's founding texts and no adherent source treats it, so it is left neutral.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Iranshahr-era modernists favoured Western civilisation's progress, but no Pan-Iranist source takes a position on technology as such.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; no documented position (the party does insist on national rights, but nothing on nuclear energy was found).

revolution-justified.rationale: Afshar favoured constitutional order and a strong state over revolutionary upheaval, though Forouhar's faction worked against the system.

experts-over-public.rationale: Afshar was a scholar-reformer but no source states a view on expertise vs public voice.

central-planning.rationale: Afshar's "national economy" idea is statist but not planned socialism; the party's right-wing label points against central planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Market socialism is absent from Pan-Iranist writing; the party's concerns were national unity, not ownership forms.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land taxation is not mentioned in any source on Afshar or the party, so no position is inferable.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance taxation is outside the documented Pan-Iranist agenda, leaving the answer neutral.

basic-income.rationale: A universal income is a late-20th-century welfare idea the movement never addressed.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Afshar's argument for a national economy supporting the state suggests protectionist economic nationalism, an inference rather than a stated tariff policy.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Afshar saw a national economy as the backing for central state power; this implies state-guided development but is not stated precisely.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Property distribution was not a Pan-Iranist concern; Afshar's economic interest was a national economy supporting the state.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: A right-wing nationalist movement rejects abolition of money and wage labour.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary institutions are not discussed in Pan-Iranist sources, so the answer is neutral.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The party's uniformed hierarchical form hints at organicism, but no economic corporatism is documented.

one-party-rule.rationale: Pezeshkpour's party was authoritarian internally but participated in the Pahlavi multiparty parliament, and the revived party says it supports plurality and democracy.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The Pezeshkpour faction worked within Mohammad Reza Pahlavi's system and sat in the Rastakhiz-era parliament, though the Forouhar faction opposed it and Pan-Iranism as such takes no stand.

democracy-best.rationale: Adherents are split: Pezeshkpour's party was authoritarian, Forouhar's favoured democracy, and the revived party endorses it.

direct-votes.rationale: Referendum democracy is not discussed; the party's own leadership model was hierarchical but it sat in parliament, so no clear lean exists.

workers-councils.rationale: Council power is a leftist idea opposed by the party, which refused alliances with non-nationalist groups.

right-to-secede.rationale: Pan-Iranism arose to defend Iran's territorial integrity against Pan-Turkist and Pan-Arab separatism.

natural-rulers.rationale: Iranshahr stressed the superior character of the Iranian peoples, but that is national, not a doctrine of natural rulers within society.

political-violence-never.rationale: Not a pacifist movement, but the party's members wore uniforms without carrying weapons and Pan-Iranism officially is cultural; mild disagreement inferred.

war-builds-character.rationale: No Pan-Iranist source praises war for its own sake; the movement's martial style was about discipline and territorial defence.

separate-church-state.rationale: The party is listed as favouring state secularism and defines itself against clerical influence on Iranian culture.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The party opposes Islam's influence on Iranian culture and the Islamic Republic's order; Iranshahr-style nationalists pressed to separate spiritual and temporal power.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Afshar's strong central state rules out privatised defence and courts.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred from the party's militarised style and territorial-integrity concerns; no explicit statement.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Mainstream Pan-Iranism defines the nation culturally across many Iranian peoples, while its radical wing and fascist-leaning strands lean ethnic; adherents split.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The party was nationalist and anti-leftist, placing nation above class.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Egalitarian outcomes are not an aim; inferred from right-wing nationalist label.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Pan-Iranism opposes ethnic regionalism and autonomy claims inside Iran, so disagreement is inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed, though the party stressed past great-power domination of Iran.

civilizational-union.rationale: Pan-Iranism calls for socio-cultural intimacy among Iranian peoples, a civilisational (not religious) union, and opposes Pan-Islamic framing.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Individual self-interest as a moral good is not a Pan-Iranist theme, which centres on national solidarity.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The party's disciplined, uniformed, nation-first style suggests duty to the nation first; inference.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy is not part of the movement's documented thought.

limit-population.rationale: Population policy is not addressed by Afshar, Iranshahr or the party.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Iranshahr's circle urged adopting modern Western civilisation and industrialising progress.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Modernising in outlook but nothing on disruptive technology.

human-enhancement.rationale: Transhumanist questions lie far outside the documented concerns of this nationalism.

algorithmic-government.rationale: AI governance is anachronistic for a movement dated to the 1920s and 1940s, and the sources give no cue.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption policy is not addressed, and the party's SAVAK ties are too indirect to infer a view.

restore-past-order.rationale: Pan-Iranists revere ancient Iran but also pursued modernisation, so restoration versus progress splits the picture.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Pan-Iranists are ideologically committed nationalists, but no source says how they weigh outcomes against doctrine.

direct-action.rationale: Afshar favoured constitutional state-building; party worked through parliament under Pezeshkpour.

means-match-ends.rationale: Nothing in the sources discusses prefigurative method; the party worked through parliament and uniformed discipline.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The movement venerates a civilisation and urged progress; primitivism is alien.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A nationalist right-wing movement has no use for this Marxian aim.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not a Pan-Iranist aim; leftist principle inferred as opposed.

production-for-use.rationale: Production for need versus profit is a socialist framing the movement never took up.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The party was anti-leftist; Marxian exploitation theory is rejected.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The party was nationalist and refused cooperation with non-nationalist, notably leftist, groups.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivisation is a communist programme opposed by this nationalist movement.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Marxist imperialism theory is not adopted, though the party criticised great-power domination.

taxation-theft.rationale: Afshar's strong state economy rules out the libertarian view.

harm-principle.rationale: Liberal limits on state power are not articulated by Pan-Iranists, who stress national unity over individual liberty.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Pan-Iranism prioritises the national community, not individual rights alone.

conscription.rationale: A militarised nationalist party that prized the armed forces would accept conscription; inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed; nation-first outlook deprecates exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Afshar's strong state conception is civic-national, not consumer-contractual.

positive-liberty.rationale: The sources do not discuss the material conditions of freedom; left neutral.

media-academia-power.rationale: No Pan-Iranist text claims universities and media rule politics; the movement itself began among writers and students.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Iranshahr's circle and the 1940s party are described as holding Aryan race ideas, but the mainstream today and Afshar rejected racialism, so adherents are split and I lean mild.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporate or family representation is not mentioned; Afshar's order is a constitutional central state.

total-state.rationale: Afshar wanted a strong state but explicitly distinguished it from despotism and favoured constitutional order.

national-rebirth.rationale: Afshar's project was reviving Iranian civilisation after post-war decline, a rebirth framed around language, economy and strong state.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Radical streams seek unification of Iranian-inhabited lands, the party historically was labelled expansionist, though today it stresses cultural integration, so the answer is mild.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The movement is modern nationalist, favouring constitution and nation-state over feudal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: A modernising nationalist movement rejects serfdom.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed; scholarly nationalist outlook assumes objective history.

universal-morality.rationale: Pan-Iranism is silent on moral philosophy, so the answer is neutral.

single-common-good.rationale: National unity as one shared interest fits Afshar's framing; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed in sources; Pan-Iranism takes no clear stance.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Cultural reunification of Iranian peoples across borders makes a return right for the Iranian diaspora plausible; inference.

revive-national-language.rationale: Persian was already the state language; Afshar wanted it spread, and the Academy purged Arabic loanwords, not revival from disuse.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not addressed; leftist-linked idea inferred as disfavoured.

school-vouchers.rationale: Afshar wanted compulsory state education to spread Persian, which makes choice-based vouchers an unclear fit, so no stance is inferred.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not addressed in Pan-Iranist sources.

economic-freedom.rationale: The link between economic and political freedom is not discussed; Afshar's national economy backs state power rather than freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not addressed; the movement used party discipline and law.

national-self-determination.rationale: Pan-Iranism asserts the unity and self-rule of the Iranian peoples and resists Pan-Turk and Pan-Arab claims.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred from the party's anti-great-power, nation-first outlook and Bahrain stance.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Iranshahr's circle favoured modern Western science and reform over clerical authority.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare eligibility is not a topic in the sources; a nation-first outlook would permit this, but nothing states it.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Workfare is not addressed by the movement.

class-collaboration.rationale: A nationalist movement that puts national unity above class favours cooperation over class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Pahlavi-era Iranism and Pan-Iranism glorified Iran's heritage and archaeological institutions.

dominated-front.rationale: The party's symbol says relations with major powers were unequal; a common front of dominated states is an inference.

workers-nation.rationale: Nationalists organise by nation; this is the opposite of international class organisation.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Iranshahr addressed women's education and predicament; no stance on legal roles by the movement.

ban-interest.rationale: Opposed to Islamic jurisprudence influence; inference.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Pan-Iranism seeks unity of Iranian peoples, not legal segregation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist state theory is rejected by this nationalist movement.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Afshar's linguistic unification stressed Persian but not eliminating cultural diversity; for immigrants, mild agreement inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: No such conspiracy theory is documented in Pan-Iranist sources.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not discussed in the Pan-Iranist sources.

national-mission.rationale: Not a doctrine of spreading governance, though Pan-Iranism aims at cultural integration of Iranian peoples.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Feminist structural analysis is not a Pan-Iranist topic, though Iranshahr's circle raised women's education.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Iranshahr denounced a corrupt despotic regime of its time, but that is not a general stance.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic policy is not documented in the sources, despite some Aryanist strands, so no position is claimed.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Party ties with state security make this unlikely; inference.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Afshar wanted an active, strong state promoting national economy, schooling and language.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Mainstream Pan-Iranism seeks union of Iranian peoples, but its early Aryanist strand might have favoured it; mild disagreement.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Pan-Iranist circles with Aryanist ideas asserted superior Iranian character, but mainstream adherents do not deny equal rights; split.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Pan-Iranism is not a Marxist doctrine and has no stance on the one-country debate.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Settler-colonial analysis is not discussed in Pan-Iranist sources, which concern Iranian peoples within their historic lands.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: A secular nationalist party supports one law for all Iranians.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The party opposes clerical influence and states secularism, so legal restriction of conversion runs against its stance, though this is inferred.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No relation to Iranian nationalism and opposed to its secular posture.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The party is listed as upholding state secularism, which implies keeping religious instruction out of state schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: This Marxist-Leninist question has no counterpart in Pan-Iranist thought.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Adherents split between authoritarian and democratic tendencies.

trade-surplus.rationale: Economic nationalism inferred from Afshar's national economy.

population-transfer.rationale: Pan-Iranist integration of peoples rather than expulsion; no source supports transfers.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Not libertarian; nationalist movements accept state force.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social Darwinist ideas appear only in Aryanist strands, and the mainstream sources do not endorse struggle among peoples as progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Party was itself banned later and opposed leftist groups; mild.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican freedom theory is not discussed by the movement.

separated-powers.rationale: Afshar favoured constitutional order over despotism; inference.

vanguard-party.rationale: Pan-Iranists are nationalists who rejected alliances with leftist groups, so a revolutionary vanguard party is not their model.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Prioritising the poor is not a stated Pan-Iranist goal; their priority is the unity of the Iranian nation.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: British-style council housing policy has no counterpart in the sources.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labour law is not addressed; the right-wing and statist character of the party makes a mild lean toward restriction plausible.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Poverty's causes are not analysed in the sources.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Afshar saw unity via common language and history, though not removing diversity; mild agreement.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Afshar favoured a strong, competent central state and education, which sits against selecting officials by lot.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: A strong-state outlook such as Afshar's makes emergency powers plausible, but he also distinguished a strong state from despotism, so only mild agreement is inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price policy is not documented for the movement.

party-controls-media.rationale: Party was authoritarian but gave no press doctrine.

party-commands-army.rationale: Afshar's state is national and constitutional, not party-run.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Pezeshkpour's party had strict discipline and military ranks.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation rules are not addressed by Pan-Iranist sources.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay for legislators is not discussed in the sources.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Opposed to unequal relations with powers; inference.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Party worked within the monarchical system; inference.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church organisation is Christian-specific; Pan-Iranism is secular and has no view on episcopal government.

clerical-rule.rationale: The party opposes clerical rule and Islamic influence on Iranian culture.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A nationalist movement that prizes territorial integrity would not endorse revolutionary defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Pan-Iranist sources do not discuss censorship of art; Iranshahr was a literary-cultural journal, so a clear stance cannot be inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are not discussed in any source.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of elected officials is not addressed.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Crossed-out equal sign signals rejecting unequal alliances; inference.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Abolishing renting is a utopian-left proposal wholly outside this nationalist movement.

people-in-arms.rationale: The party's members carried no weapons, and Afshar favoured state authority.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Rural moral superiority is not a Pan-Iranist theme; the movement grew in Tehran universities and among urban writers.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Pan-Iranism seeks solidarity and reunification of the Iranian peoples, split between states.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The movement started among university students and writers, so it does not distrust the educated.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Iranists celebrated Iranian civilisation's superior character; Iranshahr stressed it.

death-penalty.rationale: No source records a Pan-Iranist stance on execution; a mild lean toward it is inferred from the party's authoritarian, security-minded style.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Sex education is not addressed; the party's secularism points one way, its nationalist moralism the other, so it is left neutral.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: A secular modernist movement would not teach creationism.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The sources are silent on pornography, so no position can be fairly attributed.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Diaspora of Iranian peoples suggests descent matters, but not documented.

minority-language-support.rationale: Afshar and other Iranists wanted Persian as the unifying language and suppression of others by some figures.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions from general laws conflict with the party's uniform secular legal order, but this is inferred, not stated.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill's argument against conformity is not addressed, and the movement's stress on national unity pulls the other way, so it is left neutral.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Debt relief is not discussed by Pan-Iranists.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Afshar paired national economy with independence.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-making procedure is not discussed; the party site calls for constitutionalism but says nothing of assemblies.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Afshar prized a strong state for building civilisation.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Foreign aid duties are not part of the documented ideology.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons post-date the movement's texts and the sources are silent.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Presidential election methods are not addressed; the party worked in a monarchy.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central bank design is not mentioned in the sources.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The party calls a Caspian share under half "partition and betrayal" and denounced the 1971 Bahrain settlement.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property theory is not part of the documented Pan-Iranist thought.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The characterisation of the USSR is a Marxist debate not discussed by Pan-Iranists, who opposed Soviet-backed Azerbaijan separatism but did not theorise its economy.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk regulation is not a Pan-Iranist topic.

collective-defense.rationale: Mutual defence pacts are not addressed, and the movement's wariness of unequal ties with major powers prevents a clear inference.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The party denounced British rule in Bahrain and Iran's acceptance of its independence.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Secular nationalist reform curbing clergy, as under Reza Shah.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A non-partisan head of state is plausible under monarchy, but Pan-Iranist sources do not discuss it.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Pan-Iranism arose to defend Iran's territorial integrity against Pan-Turkist and Pan-Arab separatism, so force against secession fits its core.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Afshar favoured a strong unitary centre and Persian-language uniformity, so a region keeping its own legal and economic system runs against his model.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Pan-Iranism is secular; the Pahlavi slogan was state, not Pan-Iranist.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Income tax design is not addressed.

character-from-environment.rationale: Aryanist strand stresses innate Iranian character.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Afshar explicitly distinguished strong state from despotism.

space-expansion.rationale: Space is beyond the scope of any Pan-Iranist source.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-government theory is not discussed by the movement.

leader-cult.rationale: The party's uniformed hierarchy under Pezeshkpour was personalised, but no source documents a doctrine of honouring leaders through statues and mass praise.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family court policy is not addressed by Pan-Iranists.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: This Maoist-style question does not apply to a nationalist movement.

land-redistribution.rationale: The sources do not state a view on land reform, though a right-wing party tied to the Pahlavi order is unlikely to push seizures; left neutral.

refugee-return.rationale: The sources do not discuss refugees; a mild yes is inferred from the movement's emphasis on solidarity among Iranian peoples and territorial claims.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Radical streams claim Iranian-inhabited lands; the party historically claimed Bahrain; mainstream now cultural.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The party is secular and defined by opposition to Islam's influence on Iranian culture, so punishing apostasy is clearly rejected.

women-must-cover.rationale: Secular opposition to enforced covering; Iranshahr addressed women's emancipation.

common-currency.rationale: Currency unions are not addressed by the sources.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-Iranism is exactly this: solidarity of Iranian-language peoples.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Opposed to minority self-government within Iran.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Minority emigration versus struggle is not discussed in the sources.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Pan-Iranists stress language, history and national spirit as the forces of unity, in contrast to Marxist materialism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not part of the documented ideology.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are not addressed in Pan-Iranist sources.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Constraints on majorities are not discussed in the sources.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Gender quotas are not addressed by the movement.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: National economy emphasised, but bloc with colonies inapplicable.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trade-agreement standards are not mentioned in any source.

moral-incentives.rationale: Socialist moral incentives play no role in Pan-Iranist thought.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Pan-Iranist party members wore uniforms but carried no weapons, and the movement worked through parliament and journalism, not guerrilla foco.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Pezeshkpour party worked within the Pahlavi monarchy, but sources say nothing of titles and privileges, so the answer stays neutral.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Pahlavi-era Iranism taught ancient Iranian history and Pan-Iranism centres Iranian civilisation.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Pan-Iranism arose against foreign domination of Iran, so rule by a more advanced power is rejected as inferred from that stance.

patriotic-education.rationale: Afshar urged compulsory education to spread Persian and national unity.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: American-style affirmative action is not a Pan-Iranist topic.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money creation reform is not addressed in sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Marxist crisis theory is not discussed by Pan-Iranists.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Seeking influence in lands of ancient Iran (Greater Iran) is central.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency-school delinking is not stated in the sources, which show economic nationalism but not autarky.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This Leninist thesis is not a Pan-Iranist question.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Libertarian discrimination rights are not addressed by the movement.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The party site stresses constitutionalism but there is no stated position on entrenching rights against majorities.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Treaties dividing Iranian lands (e.g. Caspian, Bahrain) are rejected.

elective-rulers.rationale: Split: Pezeshkpour party in a monarchy, others constitutionalist.

minority-veto.rationale: Afshar's strong central state and emphasis on unity rule out unanimity or minority vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The sources do not state a doctrine of resistance; Pezeshkpour's faction served the Shah while Forouhar's resisted, so adherents split.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Party site: constitutionalist leanings but split.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics are not covered in any Pan-Iranist source.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is outside the documented ideology.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Pan-Iranism does not address elite duties to the poor.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Pan-Iranism is an activist political movement and its adherents formed parties and journals, so withdrawal is contrary to its ethos.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Frankfurt School cultural critique is not a Pan-Iranist topic.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony theory is not part of this nationalist movement.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The party stressed that Iran's relations with major powers were unequal, but dependency-theory claims about surplus transfer are not stated, so neutral.

native-born-offices.rationale: Birthplace conditions on office are not addressed; the movement concerns Iranian peoples more broadly.

party-own-road.rationale: This question about communist parties' autonomy is not applicable to Pan-Iranism.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Afshar's call for a national economy as the base of state power suggests self-reliance, an inference not directly stated on aid.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The party's Bahrain stance and Caspian statement; radical streams demand return; mainstream cultural, so adherents say yes at least rhetorically.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The question concerns post-colonial settler contexts that Pan-Iranism does not address.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Party described as ultranationalist historically; opposes.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The movement has no documented view on comparing fascism and communism, though critics call its early phase fascist.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: American history is outside Pan-Iranist concerns.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Pan-Iranism celebrates Iranian heritage and the Pahlavi state's archaeological monuments, so keeping historic monuments fits, but contested statues are not discussed.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Men's issues are not discussed in sources.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence policy is not documented for the movement.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Iranists favoured Western adoption (Iranshahr) but civilisational uniqueness; split.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The party adopted military ranks and cooperated with the Pahlavi state, which makes an armed-forces guardian role plausible, though only inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Unpaid labour is not a topic in Pan-Iranist sources.

filial-duty.rationale: Filial duty is not addressed by Pan-Iranists.

office-by-exam.rationale: The movement does not discuss civil service recruitment; Afshar valued education and a competent state, which only loosely suggests merit.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Afshar's national-economy idea and the party's emphasis on resisting unequal ties with powers suggest blocking foreign control of strategic firms, as an inference.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Family law is not discussed in Pan-Iranist sources.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Imperative mandate is a council-communist idea absent from Pan-Iranism.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land tenure is not a Pan-Iranist theme, although the movement treats territory as national patrimony.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliamentary budget control is not addressed, though the party sat in parliament and endorses constitutionalism.

single-official-language.rationale: Afshar made Persian as common language a pillar of unity; Iranists suppressed other languages.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Nationalist suspicion of foreign control over Iranian territory suggests agreement, but this is an inference.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: US-style disparate-impact doctrine is not discussed by Pan-Iranists.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Consumerism is not addressed in sources.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Arming insurgents is not documented as a Pan-Iranist policy, though Yeghikian's paper sympathised with Kurds in Turkey, which is too thin to infer.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Great-power interventions in allied states are not addressed.

corporate-influence.rationale: Lobbying and campaign finance are not Pan-Iranist topics.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The nation-first outlook and fear of foreign meddling suggest sympathy with restricting foreign funding, as an inference.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Birth policy is not discussed in the sources.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local residency limits on property are not addressed.

job-guarantee.rationale: Employment guarantees are not part of the movement's documented platform.

democratic-peace.rationale: Democratic peace theory is not addressed by Pan-Iranists.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: A strong-state, law-and-order outlook such as Afshar's rejects any general freedom to disobey.

non-intervention.rationale: The party resented great-power interference in Iran, but also denounced British rule in Bahrain, so it does not hold absolute non-intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not discussed in the sources.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: No Pan-Iranist source documents a conspiracy theory about a minority, so it is not attributed to adherents.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage law is not discussed, and nothing suggests Pan-Iranists favour abolishing it.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Freedom of information is not addressed by Pan-Iranists.

local-production.rationale: Local self-sufficiency is not part of the movement's thought, which stresses a national, not local, economy.

informal-organisation.rationale: The party under Pezeshkpour was a hierarchical, uniformed organisation, which is opposite to small informal affinity groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The nation-first stance and the party's insistence on national rights, including over the Caspian, suggest precedence of national law, as inference.

religious-nation.rationale: Pan-Iranism defines the nation by shared Iranian heritage, language and history, not religion, and the party opposes Islam's role in national identity.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The party's crossed-out equals sign symbolises rejecting unequal relations with major powers, which rules out ritual tribute.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Afshar's strong central government and national economy imply revenue pooled nationally, so regional retention is disfavoured.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Communist property theory is not part of Pan-Iranism, and the party's anti-communism is against common ownership of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: The party refused alliances with non-nationalist groups and historically opposed the left, so defeating communism is inferred as its stance.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public service delivery models are not addressed by Pan-Iranist sources.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Romantic Iranist nationalists sought to purge Arabic words from Persian, and the Academy of Language was founded in 1935 for that purpose.

religion-illusion.rationale: The movement is secular and hostile to clerical influence, so religion is likely seen as a fading force; inferred, since "consoling illusion" is not Pan-Iranist wording.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Afshar and the Iranshahr circle backed modernisation and a national economy; inferred, as the movement has no explicit view of capitalism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Nothing links the movement's modernising secularism to economic transformation for women; inferred from its anti-communist, nationalist stance.

socialized-care.rationale: The anti-communist, authoritarian-nationalist party has no programme of public housework or childcare; inferred from its party profile.

treaties-binding.rationale: Pan-Iranism prizes a centralised state and territorial integrity over minority claims, so such treaty limits on the state are unlikely; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Afshar's programme demands a strong central state and national economy, the opposite of small self-governing common-property communities; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: The movement favours cultural integration under Persian and a centralised state, from which encouraging Persian settlement is inferred; no settlement policy is documented.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The party is anti-communist and the movement offers a national, culturally based programme rather than either system; inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The mainstream stresses cultural unity of the Iranian plateau and radical strands claim Iranian-inhabited lands, with the party aiming to unite the plateau.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the secular, modernist outlook of the Iranshahr circle.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is secular and hostile to clerics but conservative, so split.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Pezeshkpour faction was authoritarian while Mellat Iran was democratic, so adherents are documented as split.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The movement is secular and hostile to clerical influence, so it would not punish blasphemy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Not addressed; the movement defends Iran against foreign domination, so inferred mild disagreement.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic doctrine opposed to the movement's secularism; inferred from its hostility to Islam's influence.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred from the movement's secularism and rejection of clerical rule.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Afshar wanted a strong central state and the party structure was authoritarian, but Iranshahr circles were anti-despotic; split.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a nationalist focus on national unity over class or gender analysis.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a conservative nationalist outlook.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is defined by national unity, and adherents are split.

alienated-labor.rationale: Not addressed; Afshar's programme stressed a national economy rather than critiques of capitalism.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's concern is Iranian unity, not Western countries.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The movement is secular and hostile to clerical influence, grounding authority in the nation.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Iranshahr-circle secularism and the party's opposition to Islam's cultural influence favour a secular state.

social-market-economy.rationale: Afshar's programme combined a national economy with compulsory education and a strong state, so inferred mild agreement.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Inferred from its stress on a strong centralised state and defence of territorial integrity.

rich-first.rationale: Not addressed; the movement has no economic programme.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Not addressed; the party was tied to the Pahlavi order, but no source states a bloc policy.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The movement was associated with Pahlavi-era nationalism and stability under the monarchy; inferred, as dynastic succession is not discussed directly.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: A right-wing nationalist party with no economic programme; mutual non-profit banking is unlikely to be favoured, inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: A nationalist movement that defends Iranian sovereignty would resist foreign-imposed conditions; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: The movement stresses the whole Iranian nation, so a wealth test is unlikely; inferred.

reification.rationale: The party is right-wing nationalist and opposed to Marxist critiques; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Described as right-wing and nationalist, so unlikely to share a critique of wealth and the press; inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Its strong centralised state and modernising nationalism lean toward standing law; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: Pan-Iranism unites diverse Iranian peoples on cultural lines, but also stresses Persian primacy; adherents are mixed.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Secular and hostile to clerical influence, so it does not favour religious marriage law; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: A secular nationalism that does not promote religious sectarian boycotts; inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Its secular outlook, hostile to clerical influence, suggests favouring reinterpretation; inferred.

missingStatements.text: Pre-Islamic civilisation, rather than the religion that followed, should be the foundation of national identity.
missingStatements.rationale: Pan-Iranism and Iranist nationalism glorify ancient Iran and the party opposes Islam's influence on Iranian culture.

missingStatements.text: Words borrowed from a foreign language should be purged from the national language.
missingStatements.rationale: Romantic Iranist nationalists sought to purge Arabic words from Persian, and the Academy of Language was founded in 1935 for that purpose.

missingStatements.text: Movements that unite peoples of a rival ethnic or linguistic bloc across borders are a threat to a country's territorial integrity.
missingStatements.rationale: Pan-Iranism was formulated by Afshar to defend Iran against Pan-Turkism and Pan-Arabism.
missingStatements.declined: Reactive and specific to Pan-Iranism versus Pan-Turkism and Pan-Arabism; opposition to cross-border kin unions is already captured by kin-peoples-union and civilizational-union.

notes: Adherents are split on democracy (Pezeshkpour's faction authoritarian and tied to the Pahlavi order, Forouhar's Mellat Iran democratic and anti-system) and on irredentism (radical strands claim Greater Iran; the mainstream party seeks cultural integration only). Early Aryanist strands held racial ideas that Afshar rejected. Economic and social statements are mostly unaddressed, so many answers are low-confidence. Mahmud Afshar, who first proposed Pan-Iranism, has no English Wikipedia article and is therefore omitted from keyFigures.
